## Overview
[Record] The Mongol khanate of the western steppe, tributary master of the Rus' lands. [Tokhtamysh](../characters/tokhtamysh.qmd) reunited it in 1380, burned Moscow in Aug 1382, and was broken by Timur in 1391 and 1395. He then fled to Vytautas. The beglerbeg [Edigu](../characters/edigu.qmd), kingmaker for Temür Qutlugh, crushed Vytautas's coalition at the Vorskla on 12 Aug 1399. Edigu raided Moscow in 1408, and died in 1419 (some say 1420), probably killed by a son of Tokhtamysh. Tokhtamysh's son Jalal ad-Din led Tatars at Grunwald. After the 1420s the Horde fractured, and Crimea broke away under Hacı Giray with Lithuanian support.

## Wants (by book)
| Book | Goal | Leverage | Red line |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | Tribute from the Rus'; punish Moscow (1382) | Cavalry | Moscow strong |
| II | Tokhtamysh: restoration. Edigu: Tokhtamysh's head, no protectorate over the steppe | Refugees' claim; Vorskla ambush (II ch. 15, 24-26) | A Christian khan |
| III | Edigu: punish Moscow; keep Lithuania off the Black Sea | Jalal ad-Din's riders for Vytautas | Lithuanian Black Sea forts |
| IV | Rival khans court Vytautas | Black Sea forts, Dashiv (IV ch. 11) | Edigu's end, 1419 |
| V | Fragmenting Horde; Crimea, Kazan | Lithuanian clients | None canonical |

## Patron Force
[Saga] [Stepių Alkis](../forces/steppe_hunger.qmd) (Erdene-Chuluu), which is not Tengri but the hunger of horizon-kings. It speaks through Tokhtamysh at Lutsk (II ch. 15), feeds on Vytautas as well as on Edigu, and shows Vytautas a golden Sarai through Henė before the Vorskla (II ch. 20).

## Internal tensions
Khan against kingmaker (Edigu against Tokhtamysh's line); Timur's invasions; Moscow's growing independence; Karaims and Tatars settled at Trakai serving Vytautas, a sign of the split.

## Notable members
[Tokhtamysh](../characters/tokhtamysh.qmd), [Edigu](../characters/edigu.qmd).
